findings.issue: The new settings scroll wrapper applies an unconditional 600px table minimum inside the desktop two-column layout, introducing avoidable horizontal scrolling at ordinary desktop widths above 1100px.
evidence: The new crawl-status-scroll ancestor activates crawl.css:5 (.crawl-status-scroll .ds-tbl { min-width:600px }) for the settings table at every viewport width.

crawl.css:1 uses 2fr/1fr columns with a 24px gap above 1100px. tokens.css defines the default sidebar as 224px; globals.css:36 adds 64px horizontal main padding; ds.css:14 gives the card 48px padding plus 2px border. PipelineShell initially expands the sidebar, and the crawling route does not automatically collapse it.

At 1200px with the ordinary expanded sidebar and closed chat, settings inner width is at most ((1200 - 224 - 64 - 24) * 2/3) - 50 = 542px. The table must therefore scroll by at least 58px. At 1101px it has only 476px, requiring at least 124px of horizontal travel. The rightmost usage controls/labels move into a horizontal scroll region despite this being desktop. The previous fixed-layout table fitted the card using cell wrapping.

At 1024px the single-column breakpoint provides 838px, and at 1440px the desktop settings card provides 702px, so checking only those two endpoints misses the regression. It occurs approximately from 1101px through 1286px with the normal sidebar.
This violates the requested desktop no-needless-horizontal-scroll criterion. The new tests pass because they assert class names and CSS strings without evaluating available component width.
findings.fix: Keep the 600px scroll treatment for narrow screens, but make the desktop settings layout provide enough table width or scope/reset the settings-table minimum at desktop breakpoints so the table fits its card. Preserve the existing progress-table behavior. Verify 375px and desktop widths around the 1100px breakpoint, especially 1200px with the expanded sidebar.

findings.issue: The new table-level nowrap declaration does not make table cell contents nowrap, and its regression assertion does not establish the intended computed style.
evidence: ds.css:170 explicitly sets .ds-tbl td,.ds-tbl th { white-space:normal; overflow-wrap:anywhere } and .ds-tbl { table-layout:fixed }.

white-space:nowrap on the ancestor table is inherited only when a cell has no explicit value; even a more specific ancestor selector cannot override the explicit normal value on the cells. Long Korean descriptions therefore continue to wrap within fixed-width columns.

channelExpansion.test.ts:154 checks only that the nowrap source declaration exists. It cannot detect this cascade interaction. The 600px minimum still creates mobile horizontal scrolling, so this observation alone is not a release blocker.
findings.fix: If nonwrapping cell content is required, target the relevant cells at the intended narrow breakpoint and verify computed styles and text visibility. Account for long Korean descriptions and fixed table layout; do not apply unbounded nowrap globally on desktop.
